description: Baseline: map current urgency probability monotonically across six horizons

asi.hypothesis: The production urgency score may provide a weak ordered-horizon baseline when mapped monotonically into six classes.
asi.learning: Urgency separates evergreen articles well (AUC 0.87) but collapses argmax predictions and gives very poor macro F1, leaving substantial room for an article-content model.

description: Multinomial logistic regression over normalized EmbeddingGemma vectors

asi.hypothesis: EmbeddingGemma vectors encode semantic lifetime cues that a regularized multinomial linear classifier can recover.
asi.learning: Embedding-only logistic regression halves RPS versus urgency mapping and improves all probability-sensitive metrics; direct semantic representation is a strong baseline despite modest hard-label kappa.

description: Increase multinomial embedding regularization with C=0.3

asi.hypothesis: Stronger regularization may smooth overconfident class probabilities and lower RPS on the temporal test split.
asi.learning: C=0.3 underfits the embedding signal: RPS, macro F1, kappa, and MAE all worsen versus C=1.0.
asi.next_action_hint: Try moderately weaker regularization or a structurally different ordinal/text model.

description: Reduce embedding logistic regularization with C=3

asi.hypothesis: The small training set still benefits from a less constrained embedding decision surface because pretrained vectors already carry strong semantic structure.
asi.learning: C=3 improves RPS by 0.0081 over C=1 and also improves every secondary metric, indicating the C=1 model was underfitting rather than overconfident.

description: Further reduce embedding logistic regularization with C=10

asi.hypothesis: A still weaker L2 penalty may recover finer semantic horizon distinctions without unacceptable probability overconfidence.
asi.learning: C=10 improves RPS, kappa, and duration MAE; evergreen AUC and macro F1 dip slightly, but the ordered probability quality improves clearly.

description: Test weak embedding logistic regularization with C=30

asi.hypothesis: C=30 may continue the C=1 to C=10 improvement trend by sharpening semantic class boundaries.
asi.learning: The RPS optimum is below C=30: confidence rises to 0.71 and duration MAE improves, but probability calibration and most classification metrics regress.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep C=10 and test ordinal decomposition or text features instead of pushing regularization further.

description: Ordinal cumulative logistic classifiers over normalized embeddings

asi.hypothesis: Five cumulative boundary classifiers align training directly with the ordered structure measured by RPS.
asi.learning: Ordinal decomposition yields a small RPS gain and clear improvements in macro F1, kappa, and evergreen AUC over multinomial C=10; monotone tail probabilities prevent invalid negative class mass.

description: Increase ordinal boundary regularization with C=3

asi.hypothesis: More regularized cumulative classifiers may improve boundary calibration.
asi.learning: As with multinomial classification, C=3 underfits; RPS and ordered hard-label metrics regress materially.
asi.next_action_hint: Try weaker ordinal regularization around C=20 or add independent lexical temporal cues.

description: Reduce ordinal boundary regularization with C=20

asi.hypothesis: Ordinal boundary models may benefit from slightly sharper fits than C=10.
asi.learning: C=20 lowers RPS and duration MAE despite small declines in hard-label metrics and evergreen AUC; probability sharpness helps overall ordered calibration.

description: Test sharper ordinal boundary fits with C=40

asi.hypothesis: C=40 may improve class separation while preserving ordinal probability quality.
asi.learning: C=40 improves kappa and duration MAE but is slightly over-sharp for RPS and lowers evergreen AUC; C=20 is the calibration optimum in this range.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep ordinal C=20; test text-only signals or an embedding/text ensemble.

description: Blend ordinal probabilities with 5% training class prior

asi.hypothesis: A small class-prior blend may reduce overconfidence and improve temporal-test calibration.
asi.learning: Prior smoothing worsens both RPS and duration MAE without changing hard decisions; the C=20 ordinal probabilities are not globally overconfident.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not apply global smoothing; add complementary lexical features.

description: Word TF-IDF multinomial classifier over titles and article bodies

asi.hypothesis: Explicit lexical date, deadline, and event words may predict horizon better than dense semantic embeddings.
asi.learning: Text-only word TF-IDF is much better than urgency but clearly worse than embeddings on RPS and every secondary metric; lexical cues may still be complementary in an ensemble.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary RPS was 0.10525204 versus 0.09039041 for ordinal embeddings.
asi.next_action_hint: Combine sparse TF-IDF with embeddings or blend text probabilities at low weight rather than replacing embeddings.

description: Blend 20% word TF-IDF predictions into ordinal embeddings

asi.hypothesis: Lexical predictions may correct embedding errors when blended conservatively.
asi.learning: A 20% text blend slightly improves hard-label metrics but worsens RPS, duration MAE, and evergreen AUC; text errors are not complementary enough at this weight.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary RPS regressed from 0.09039041 to 0.09203494 and added substantial complexity.
asi.next_action_hint: If revisited, try direct feature concatenation or at most a very small text weight; prioritize simpler explicit temporal features.

description: Concatenate word TF-IDF with embeddings for ordinal classification

asi.hypothesis: Joint linear boundary models can use lexical cues only when they add information beyond embeddings.
asi.learning: Adding 5k TF-IDF features increases confidence and slightly improves duration MAE, but RPS and evergreen discrimination regress; sparse lexical detail overfits the small training set.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary RPS regressed from 0.09039041 to 0.09254488 with much higher feature dimensionality.
asi.next_action_hint: Use a tiny fixed temporal feature set instead of thousands of lexical dimensions.

description: Append fixed temporal phrase flags to ordinal embeddings

asi.hypothesis: A small hand-chosen multilingual temporal vocabulary may add deadline and recency cues missing from dense embeddings.
asi.learning: Temporal flags raise weighted kappa strongly but worsen RPS and evergreen AUC; binary phrase presence sharpens some hard decisions while harming probability ranking.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary RPS regressed from 0.09039041 to 0.09139687 and the added vocabulary increases maintenance complexity.
asi.next_action_hint: Avoid hand-maintained cue lists unless a much smaller or cross-validated formulation improves RPS.

description: Balance classes independently at each ordinal boundary

asi.hypothesis: Boundary class imbalance may suppress rare short horizons, so balanced losses could improve ordered predictions.
asi.learning: Full balancing greatly improves macro F1 and kappa but badly degrades RPS and duration calibration; optimized class frequencies encode useful priors that should not be erased.
asi.next_action_hint: If class reweighting is revisited, use a mild fractional correction rather than fully balanced weights.

description: Apply quarter-power class balancing to ordinal boundaries

asi.hypothesis: A mild quarter-power correction can recover minority-boundary signal without discarding empirical class priors.
asi.learning: Fractional balancing lowers RPS by 0.00138 and substantially improves kappa, unlike full balancing; gentle prior correction is useful while alpha=1 is too aggressive.

description: Reduce ordinal class-balance correction exponent to one eighth

asi.hypothesis: A smaller imbalance correction may retain more calibration while still helping rare boundaries.
asi.learning: Alpha 0.125 gives slightly better macro F1 and MAE but worse RPS than alpha 0.25; the stronger quarter-power correction better matches ordered probability errors.
asi.next_action_hint: Test alpha 0.375 to locate whether the optimum lies above 0.25.

description: Increase ordinal class-balance correction exponent to three eighths

asi.hypothesis: A slightly stronger fractional balance than one quarter may improve rare-boundary ranking without the calibration damage of full balancing.
asi.learning: Alpha 0.375 gives a small RPS gain and large macro F1/kappa gains; the calibration optimum is between mild and full balancing.

description: Use square-root class balancing at ordinal boundaries

asi.hypothesis: Square-root balancing may be the midpoint between empirical and fully balanced boundary priors.
asi.learning: Alpha 0.5 passes the optimum: RPS, macro F1, kappa, and MAE all regress versus alpha 0.375 despite a negligible AUC gain.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep alpha 0.375; tune model regularization jointly or test another representation.

description: Increase regularization for fractionally balanced ordinal models with C=10

asi.hypothesis: Fractional class weighting may require stronger regularization than the unweighted optimum.
asi.learning: C=10 underfits ordered probabilities and duration, though it slightly improves evergreen AUC; alpha 0.375 still prefers C=20.
asi.next_action_hint: Test C=30 or 40 with alpha 0.375 to bracket the joint optimum.

description: Reduce regularization for fractionally balanced ordinal models with C=30

asi.hypothesis: A sharper C=30 fit may improve the fractionally balanced boundary probabilities.
asi.learning: C=30 is effectively tied but marginally worse on RPS and clearly worse on macro F1/kappa; C=20 remains simpler and better calibrated.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary RPS increased by 0.00001663 and no secondary tradeoff justified keeping it.
asi.next_action_hint: Stop tuning C around 20; test PCA, centroids, or urgency blending.

description: Append production urgency probability to embedding features

asi.hypothesis: The separately trained urgency probability may add a compact orthogonal signal to semantic embeddings.
asi.learning: Urgency adds no useful information beyond the same underlying embeddings and degrades RPS, duration MAE, and evergreen AUC.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not reuse production urgency in the intrinsic model; focus on representation geometry.

description: Whiten embeddings through 64-component PCA before ordinal classification

asi.hypothesis: PCA whitening may remove noisy embedding directions and improve temporal generalization.
asi.learning: Compressing to 64 whitened components loses useful lifetime structure and worsens every probability-sensitive metric; L2 regularization in the full embedding space is preferable.
asi.next_action_hint: Avoid aggressive dimensionality reduction; try a distance-based or ridge-regression ordinal model.

description: Ridge regression on cumulative horizon targets with alpha=1

asi.hypothesis: Multi-output ridge regression directly minimizes the squared cumulative errors used by RPS.
asi.learning: Direct squared-loss cumulative regression improves evergreen AUC but underfits class ordering and trails logistic boundaries on RPS; alpha=1 may be too strong.
asi.next_action_hint: Try weaker ridge alpha once because the direct objective is promising, then abandon if still behind.

description: Reduce cumulative ridge regularization to alpha=0.1

asi.hypothesis: A weaker ridge penalty may recover the semantic boundary detail lost at alpha=1.
asi.learning: Alpha 0.1 improves hard ordering versus alpha=1 but barely improves RPS and sharply harms evergreen AUC; squared-loss regression is inferior to logistic boundaries here.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary RPS remains far above the 0.08881373 logistic result.
asi.next_action_hint: Abandon ridge; spend remaining runs on nearest-centroid evidence or conservative refinements to the best model.

description: Shrinkage linear discriminant analysis over normalized embeddings

asi.hypothesis: Covariance-aware linear discriminant analysis may exploit embedding geometry beyond independent logistic boundaries.
asi.learning: Shrinkage LDA is extremely overconfident (0.95) and has poor RPS despite excellent expected-duration MAE; its probabilities are unsuitable without heavy calibration.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not pursue covariance models on 266 rows; retain regularized logistic boundaries.

description: Five-fold sigmoid calibration for each ordinal boundary

asi.hypothesis: Training-only cross-validated sigmoid calibration may improve cumulative boundary probabilities.
asi.learning: Calibration improves evergreen AUC but worsens RPS, kappa, and MAE; fold-level fitting loses more semantic signal than the sigmoid correction recovers.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary RPS regressed from 0.08881373 to 0.08984338 and model complexity increased substantially.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the direct probability outputs; use remaining runs for a tiny coefficient refinement or validation repeat.

description: Refine fractional class-balance exponent from 0.375 to 0.35

asi.hypothesis: Quadratic interpolation of tested exponents suggests the local RPS optimum is near 0.35.
asi.learning: The measured gain is only 0.0000096 with unchanged hard metrics, far below a meaningful effect and likely benchmark-specific; retaining the interpretable three-eighths setting better avoids test-set overfitting.
asi.rollback_reason: Discarded despite nominal primary improvement because it is negligible, test-tuned, and below the prompt's 0.001 equivalence threshold.
asi.next_action_hint: Use the final run to confirm the retained best deterministically rather than tuning another decimal.

description: Determinism check of retained ordinal embedding model

asi.hypothesis: The retained model and fixed harness should reproduce bit-for-bit before ending the initial segment.
asi.learning: All six metrics exactly match experiment 19, confirming deterministic training, prediction, and evaluation.
asi.rollback_reason: No code change and no primary improvement; logged as a validation run only.
asi.next_action_hint: Review the retained model on a new frozen temporal holdout or human-audited labels before further hyperparameter tuning.

description: Retained ordinal embedding model as structural-search baseline

asi.hypothesis: The best deterministic model from the first segment is the correct baseline for a new structural-model segment.
asi.learning: The retained model reproduces all prior metrics exactly; this segment will avoid fine-grained test-tuned hyperparameters and only compare materially different formulations.

description: Append one-hot feed identity to ordinal embedding features

asi.hypothesis: Feed identity may encode a stable source-level lifetime prior that complements article semantics.
asi.learning: Feed identity improves macro F1, kappa, and evergreen AUC but slightly worsens RPS and duration MAE; source priors do not improve overall ordered calibration and risk source-specific overfitting.
asi.next_action_hint: Avoid source identity; test source-agnostic two-stage or non-linear semantic formulations.

description: Two-stage evergreen then conditional mutable-horizon classification

asi.hypothesis: Separating evergreen detection from mutable-horizon prediction may prevent evergreen rows from distorting short-horizon boundaries.
asi.learning: Two-stage training nominally lowers RPS by 0.00069 and MAE, but materially worsens macro F1 and kappa while nearly doubling code; the gain is below the prompt's 0.001 equivalence threshold.
asi.rollback_reason: Prefer the simpler one-stage ordinal model for a sub-threshold gain and avoid fitting architecture to one frozen test split.
asi.next_action_hint: Explore genuinely different low-complexity geometry such as kernel approximation or nearest neighbors.

description: Cosine 25-nearest-neighbor horizon probabilities

asi.hypothesis: Semantically nearby articles may share lifetime even when the relationship is not linearly separable.
asi.learning: Local cosine neighborhoods generalize poorly across the temporal split and trail linear embeddings on every metric; article lifetime is a broad semantic direction, not local story similarity.
asi.next_action_hint: Skip neighbor-count tuning; test a compact non-linear kernel model or class centroids only if it remains simple.

description: RBF support-vector classifiers at ordinal boundaries

asi.hypothesis: A smooth non-linear boundary may capture interactions among semantic embedding dimensions missed by logistic regression.
asi.learning: RBF boundaries worsen RPS and all classification metrics; with 266 temporal training rows the extra flexibility does not generalize.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not tune kernels on this test set; return to linear models and seek target/feature formulations.

description: Ordinal word TF-IDF classifiers over titles only

asi.hypothesis: Titles may concentrate deadlines and event state while avoiding evergreen background text in article bodies.
asi.learning: Title vocabulary alone is far too sparse and temporally unstable; it performs worse than body-inclusive TF-IDF and dense embeddings on every metric.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not add title-only ensembles; dense semantics remain essential.

description: Ten-component partial least squares on cumulative targets

asi.hypothesis: Supervised low-rank projection may isolate a few semantic lifetime directions and reduce high-dimensional variance.
asi.learning: PLS loses evergreen discrimination and worsens RPS; useful lifetime information is distributed beyond ten supervised components or is better regularized by logistic loss.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not tune PLS component counts on the fixed test set; investigate training-only model selection or bagging.

description: Twenty-model bootstrap bagging at each ordinal boundary

asi.hypothesis: Bootstrap averaging may reduce variance from the small temporal training set without changing the linear semantic model.
asi.learning: Bagging slightly improves MAE and evergreen AUC but marginally worsens RPS and sharply lowers hard-label quality; full-data fitting is more valuable than variance reduction here.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary RPS increased and 100 fitted models add unjustified complexity for a near tie.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep one full-data model; consider training-only validation to choose boundary-specific regularization rather than test-wide constants.

description: Select boundary C values on newest training quarter

asi.hypothesis: A chronological validation slice within training can choose regularization without tuning against frozen test labels.
asi.learning: Training-only selection chose C=[10,3,3,10,10], but these stronger penalties underfit the later test period and worsen RPS/MAE; the tiny validation slice is too noisy for per-boundary selection.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary RPS regressed from 0.08881373 to 0.09034071 and code complexity rose sharply.
asi.next_action_hint: Retain one global regularization value; try label smoothing or adjacent-class targets derived entirely from training labels.

description: Mean-center embeddings before L2 normalization

asi.hypothesis: Removing the dominant mean embedding direction may expose semantic lifetime geometry hidden by anisotropy.
asi.learning: Centering gives the best duration MAE seen among linear models but produces sharper, worse-calibrated probabilities and lower AUC; it may offer complementary expected-duration signal.
asi.next_action_hint: Test one conservative blend of centered and uncentered ordinal probabilities, then stop if RPS does not improve materially.

description: Blend 20% mean-centered ordinal probabilities

asi.hypothesis: A small centered-embedding component may add complementary duration structure without dominating calibration.
asi.learning: The blend nominally improves RPS by only 0.000056 plus kappa/MAE, but lowers evergreen AUC and doubles model fits; the primary gain is far below the 0.001 simplicity threshold.
asi.rollback_reason: Discarded a negligible benchmark-specific gain to preserve the simpler one-representation model and avoid blend-weight tuning.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not tune the blend weight; investigate removing common principal components using training-only geometry only if it can stay simple.

description: Center embeddings and remove their top principal component

asi.hypothesis: The common top embedding direction may be corpus noise that obscures semantic lifetime.
asi.learning: The leading centered component carries essential freshness information: removing it sharply degrades every metric, especially evergreen AUC.
asi.next_action_hint: Preserve the full embedding geometry; do not remove additional components.

description: Ridge regression to one latent horizon with Gaussian class spread

asi.hypothesis: A single continuous lifetime direction may generalize better than five independently fitted boundaries.
asi.learning: The proportional one-score assumption underfits the class-specific semantic boundaries and produces excessively diffuse distributions; RPS and MAE regress.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep independent cumulative boundaries; inspect alternative linear losses rather than collapsing to one score.

description: L1-sparse logistic models at ordinal boundaries

asi.hypothesis: Sparse coefficients may select a compact set of embedding dimensions that generalizes across time.
asi.learning: L1 sparsity damages probability calibration, MAE, and evergreen discrimination; freshness information is distributed across embedding dimensions rather than axis-aligned.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not tune sparse penalties; retain dense L2 weights.

description: Append parsed duration and explicit-date features to embeddings

asi.hypothesis: Numeric durations and explicit dates interpreted relative to publication can add concrete lifetime evidence beyond dense semantics.
asi.learning: Parsed temporal features substantially improve weighted kappa but slightly worsen RPS and evergreen AUC; they sharpen ordinal decisions without improving probability calibration.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary RPS regressed and 80+ lines of parsing complexity are unjustified for a near tie under the 0.001 simplicity rule.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not tune feature weights on the test set; preserve this as evidence that explicit dates may matter in a larger human-labeled corpus.

description: Balanced ExtraTrees classifier over embeddings

asi.hypothesis: Randomized trees may recover non-linear semantic interactions without kernel tuning.
asi.learning: Axis-aligned trees underfit dense distributed embeddings and produce diffuse, poorly ordered probabilities; all metrics regress.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not tune tree ensembles on dense embeddings.

description: Project crossing ordinal probabilities with isotonic regression

asi.hypothesis: Least-squares isotonic projection should repair crossing boundary probabilities more faithfully than asymmetrically clipping every later tail downward.
asi.learning: Proper PAVA projection lowers RPS by 0.00089 and MAE with identical hard predictions and AUC; it directly matches the ordered squared-error objective and adds only one standard sklearn operation.

description: Determinism check for isotonic ordinal projection

asi.hypothesis: The retained isotonic improvement should reproduce exactly despite the dashboard's cross-experiment noise estimate.
asi.learning: All metrics reproduce bit-for-bit; the 0.00089 gain is deterministic, though external-holdout significance still requires new labels.
asi.rollback_reason: No code change or additional primary improvement; validation run only.
asi.next_action_hint: Continue with non-test-tuned probability constraints or training-only targets.

description: Normalize fractional class weights to unit mean per boundary

asi.hypothesis: Unit-mean class weights should keep C's effective regularization comparable across differently imbalanced boundaries.
asi.learning: Weight normalization slightly improves duration MAE but marginally worsens RPS with identical hard predictions; the original implicit per-boundary regularization is better calibrated.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary RPS increased and added bookkeeping for a negligible tradeoff.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the original fractional weights; avoid further decimal-scale weighting changes.

description: Blend 20% multinomial probabilities into ordinal predictions

asi.hypothesis: A multinomial classifier may add mutually exclusive class evidence missing from independently fitted ordinal boundaries.
asi.learning: The multinomial component slightly improves evergreen AUC but worsens RPS, MAE, macro F1, and kappa; its errors are not complementary enough.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary RPS regressed and an extra model adds complexity.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not tune multinomial blend weights; the isotonic ordinal model remains stronger alone.

description: Character TF-IDF ordinal classifiers over title and body

asi.hypothesis: Character n-grams may capture multilingual temporal morphology, dates, and recurring phrases more robustly than word TF-IDF.
asi.learning: Character text features improve over title-only words but remain far behind dense embeddings on every metric; surface patterns do not generalize enough across time.
asi.next_action_hint: Stop text-only variants; semantic embeddings are decisively better.

description: Class-prior-adjusted cosine similarity to horizon centroids

asi.hypothesis: One semantic centroid per horizon may provide a stable low-variance alternative for rare classes.
asi.learning: Horizon classes are not compact cosine clusters; centroid probabilities collapse hard ordering and severely regress RPS despite retaining some evergreen ranking.
asi.next_action_hint: Close the centroid/nearest-neighbor hypothesis; discriminative linear boundaries are necessary.

description: Move 10% probability mass to adjacent horizons

asi.hypothesis: Adjacent-class smoothing can express teacher horizon uncertainty without moving mass to semantically distant classes.
asi.learning: Smoothing nominally lowers RPS by only 0.000028 and raises AUC, but worsens F1, kappa, and MAE; the tiny gain is not robust enough to justify a fixed smoothing constant.
asi.rollback_reason: Discarded a sub-noise, test-specific primary gain under the 0.001 simplicity and anti-overfitting rule.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not tune smoothing strength on this holdout.

description: Regularized 32-unit MLP over embeddings

asi.hypothesis: A tiny hidden layer may capture semantic interactions while early stopping controls overfitting.
asi.learning: The MLP severely underfits the small imbalanced dataset and produces nearly uninformative probabilities; neural fine-tuning is unsupported at this sample size.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not tune neural architectures in this local benchmark.

description: Proportional-odds logistic model with shared semantic slope

asi.hypothesis: A proper proportional-odds model can reduce variance by sharing one embedding direction across all horizon thresholds.
asi.learning: Shared slopes retain ordered hard predictions but sharply reduce evergreen AUC and worsen RPS; different horizon boundaries require distinct semantic directions.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary RPS regressed from 0.08792380 to 0.09088882 with more data reshaping complexity.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep independent boundary coefficients; shared-slope ordinal models are too restrictive.

description: Non-ensemble five-fold sigmoid boundary calibration

asi.hypothesis: Cross-validated sigmoid calibration with a final full-data estimator may avoid the signal loss of fold-ensemble calibration.
asi.learning: Full-data calibrated estimators improve over fold ensembles but still worsen RPS and hard-label quality; logistic outputs plus PAVA are better calibrated directly.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary RPS regressed from 0.08792380 to 0.08935971 and fitting cost/complexity rose.
asi.next_action_hint: Close probability calibration variants on this sample size.

description: Modified-Huber SGD classifiers at ordinal boundaries

asi.hypothesis: Modified-Huber loss may resist noisy teacher labels while preserving decisive semantic boundaries.
asi.learning: Robust margins produce excellent expected-duration MAE but severe overconfidence and worse RPS/AUC; probability quality, not boundary location, is the failure.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not tune SGD losses; log-loss remains necessary for calibrated probabilities.

description: RBF kernel ridge on cumulative horizon targets

asi.hypothesis: Kernel ridge can optimize squared cumulative targets directly while modeling smooth non-linear semantic effects.
asi.learning: Non-linear Brier regression improves over linear ridge but still trails logistic boundaries on RPS and all classification metrics; direct squared loss remains less effective.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not tune kernel parameters against the fixed test set.

description: One-vs-rest logistic classifiers for exact horizons

asi.hypothesis: Independent exact-class classifiers may preserve rare-class evidence better than multinomial competition.
asi.learning: One-vs-rest exact classes underperform cumulative boundaries on every metric; explicitly encoding order remains essential.
asi.next_action_hint: Close unordered exact-class formulations.

description: Five-percent soft targets at ordinal boundaries

asi.hypothesis: Soft binary targets can absorb teacher-label uncertainty during fitting rather than post-hoc smoothing.
asi.learning: Training label smoothing makes boundaries too diffuse and worsens RPS, MAE, and hard-label metrics; direct hard pseudo-labels generalize better.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not tune smoothing strength on this holdout.

description: ANOVA-select 256 embedding dimensions before ordinal fitting

asi.hypothesis: Supervised filtering may remove embedding dimensions unrelated to horizon while preserving broad semantic axes.
asi.learning: ANOVA selection improves evergreen AUC and kappa but worsens RPS, macro F1, and MAE; univariate class association discards useful distributed calibration signal.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary RPS regressed and choosing feature counts on this holdout would overfit.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not sweep feature counts; retain all embedding dimensions.

description: Prior-smooth semantically unfamiliar test articles

asi.hypothesis: Test articles outside the training embedding neighborhood should receive more conservative class-prior probabilities.
asi.learning: Cosine unfamiliarity is not a useful calibration proxy: adaptive smoothing worsens RPS, kappa, and MAE while leaving AUC unchanged.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary RPS regressed and transductive distance logic adds complexity.
asi.next_action_hint: Close abstention-by-embedding-distance; model confidence is not improved by local density.

description: Append smoothed feed-level cumulative horizon priors

asi.hypothesis: Smoothed source-level horizon rates may add stable context without the high variance of one-hot feed coefficients.
asi.learning: Target-encoded feed priors improve every quality metric, including RPS by 0.00032, but the gain is below the 0.001 simplicity threshold and relies on source-specific history rather than article semantics.
asi.rollback_reason: Discarded to avoid benchmark/source overfitting and roughly doubling code for a sub-threshold gain.
asi.next_action_hint: Reconsider source priors only on a larger external holdout where unseen-feed behavior can be measured.

description: Remove redundant embedding normalization

asi.hypothesis: Frozen EmbeddingGemma vectors may already be unit-normalized, making runtime normalization redundant.
asi.learning: Raw and normalized embeddings produce metrics equal to numerical precision, while removing an import and two preprocessing calls; the simpler candidate is preferable under the 0.001 equivalence rule.

description: Remove unused logistic random seed

asi.hypothesis: The deterministic LBFGS solver does not use LogisticRegression.random_state.
asi.learning: All metrics remain bit-for-bit identical after removing the unused argument; deterministic behavior is preserved with less configuration.

description: Use default logistic iteration limit

asi.hypothesis: The five small LBFGS fits converge within sklearn's default iteration limit.
asi.learning: All metrics remain identical and checks emit no convergence warning; the explicit 2000-iteration override was unnecessary.

description: Remove per-boundary logistic intercepts

asi.hypothesis: Fractional class weights already encode boundary priors, so free intercepts may redundantly fit the small teacher sample.
asi.learning: Disabling intercepts removes five fitted parameters while lowering RPS by 0.00054 and improving evergreen AUC with unchanged hard predictions; the simpler constrained model generalizes better.

description: Determinism check for intercept-free ordinal model

asi.hypothesis: The intercept-free gain should reproduce exactly before further changes.
asi.learning: All metrics reproduce bit-for-bit, confirming the constrained solver is deterministic.
asi.rollback_reason: No code change or new primary improvement; validation run only.
asi.next_action_hint: Continue seeking parameter-removing constraints rather than adding features.

description: Remove fractional class balancing

asi.hypothesis: The intercept-free model may make explicit class weighting unnecessary, enabling a much smaller candidate.
asi.learning: Removing weights improves duration MAE but degrades RPS by 0.00222 and sharply harms macro F1/kappa; fractional balancing remains essential beyond the simplicity tolerance.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regression exceeds the 0.001 equivalence threshold despite fewer lines.
asi.next_action_hint: Retain fractional weights; simplify only arguments that are demonstrably redundant.

description: Replace isotonic projection with cumulative clipping

asi.hypothesis: The original one-line cumulative clipping may be preferable if its RPS remains within the session's explicit 0.001 simplicity tolerance.
asi.learning: Removing isotonic regression costs 0.000969 RPS with identical F1, kappa, and AUC, while deleting an import and multi-row projection; this is just inside the declared equivalence threshold.
asi.tradeoff: Accepted a bounded primary regression to follow the prompt's explicit preference for less code when RPS differs by under 0.001.

description: Generate boundary class weights from counts

asi.hypothesis: A count-driven comprehension can express the same fractional balancing without duplicated formulas and named positive/negative variables.
asi.learning: Metrics remain identical; the shorter symmetric weight construction is behavior-preserving.

description: Smooth neighboring ordinal boundary coefficients

asi.hypothesis: A fixed three-point average across neighboring boundary coefficient vectors may reduce variance while retaining boundary-specific semantic directions.
asi.learning: Coefficient sharing improves macro F1, kappa, and evergreen AUC but makes probabilities too diffuse and worsens RPS/MAE; independent boundary slopes are needed for calibration.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary RPS regressed from 0.08835420 to 0.09210295 and added substantial post-fit logic.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not tune the smoothing weight on this holdout; retain independent coefficients.
